personality: 7 Dark-First Utility with neon gaming accents
personality_one_liner: A high-octane, neon-drenched rhythm command center that feels fast, tactile, and effortlessly cool.

spacing.rule: Generous margins for touch targets, tight spacing for dense rhythm metrics.

do's: Use heavy glass over the animated equalizer background for menus
Use glass for HUD elements during gameplay so the highway isn't obscured
Apply high-opacity tint (≥75% surface) beneath blur to guarantee text readability
dont's: Don't blur the actual 3D gameplay canvas
Don't use weak blur that makes text hard to read against neon backgrounds

screens.name: Home
screens.purpose: Main menu hub featuring an animated neon visualizer and clear calls-to-action.

states.loading: Pulsing neon logo with equalizer bars.
states.error: Glass modal with red glowing border and retry button.

screens.layout: Background: Animated audio visualizer (image/canvas). Foreground: Full-screen glassmorphism layout with safe areas. Large, high-impact typography for the 'Vocotap' logo. A centered column of chunky, pill-shaped buttons for 'Play', 'Library', 'Settings', and 'Tutorial'. Music-app-like minimalism mixed with arcade aesthetics.

screens.name: Library (Song Select)
screens.purpose: Browse, filter, and select songs from on-device or Treesh Music.

states.loading: Skeleton grid with shimmering glass effect.
states.empty: Illustration of an unplugged cable; 'No songs found. Import audio to begin.'
states.error: Failed to load library - Retry button.

screens.layout: Beatstar-style clean hub. Sticky top header with Search and Filter chips (BPM, Difficulty). Grid of song cards. Each card has album artwork (or gradient placeholder), title, difficulty badge (Easy/Normal/Hard/Expert colored), and a 'Play' CTA. Import button fixed at bottom.

screens.name: Gameplay
screens.purpose: The core rhythm experience: 4-lane perspective highway with HUD.
screens.layout: Full-bleed Canvas/WebGL for the 3D 4-lane highway. React Native HUD overlay using glass panels. Top Left: Score & Combo. Top Right: Pause button. Bottom edges: Rock meter (fail state) and Vocopulse meter. Judgment popups (Perfect/Great/Miss) float dynamically in the center.

screens.name: Results
screens.purpose: Post-song score summary and performance breakdown.
screens.layout: Cinematic modal over a blurred snapshot of the last gameplay frame. Giant star rating (up to 5 stars). Large score display. Detailed breakdown of Perfect/Great/Good/Miss hits. Primary CTA: 'Continue', Secondary: 'Replay' or 'Edit Chart'.

screens.name: Chart Editor
screens.purpose: Complex, dense command-center for creating and editing rhythm charts.

states.loading: Analyzing waveform and generating beat grid...

screens.layout: Landscape-optimized (or dense portrait). Scrolling 4-lane timeline over a real-time waveform. Toolbar at the bottom with tools: Tap, Hold, Wavy, Erase. Zoom controls and Snap-to-beat toggles. Sticky 'Test' and 'Save' buttons at the top right.

screens.name: Analysis & Import
screens.purpose: Visual feedback while the auto-charting engine analyzes uploaded audio.

states.loading: Real-time FFT waveform animation scanning the track.

screens.layout: Focused, distraction-free screen. Large circular progress indicator with a scanning laser line over a waveform. Readouts for BPM, density, and estimated difficulty updating live.

screens.name: Calibration & Settings
screens.purpose: Fine-tune latency, offset, and device performance.
screens.layout: List-based UI. Sliders for audio offset and note speed. Toggles for haptics, hit SFX, and No Fail mode. A live interactive tap-test area at the top for instant visual/audio sync feedback.

home_background.alt: Abstract neon red and blue audio visualizer background

instructions_to_main_agent: Implement the '7 Dark-First Utility' personality with Neon accents. The app MUST NOT feel like a generic React Native form; it must feel like a premium mobile game hub.
Use Rajdhani for all numbers, scores, and large headings to give it a tech/cyberpunk feel.
Implement the gameplay engine (Canvas/WebGL) as a full-bleed background or WebView, with React Native Expo components overlaying it as a HUD using absolute positioning and glassmorphism.

For the home screen, use the provided `home_background` image with a heavy `expo-linear-gradient` scrim (top to bottom, transparent to 90% surfaceInverse) so that menu text remains perfectly readable.
The Library screen should mimic Beatstar's clean, music-app-like interface: grid or list with large album art, bold titles, and clear difficulty badges (Easy/Normal/Hard/Expert colored).
Wire up haptics meticulously. A rhythm game lives and dies on tactile feedback. See the `haptics` block.
The Chart Editor is complex. Prioritize a scrolling timeline with a visible beat grid. Ensure touch targets for placing notes are generous (≥44pt).
Avoid standard system UI components like default alerts. Use custom frosted glass modals with neon borders (borderStrong) for all alerts and results.
